newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO GROUND BAN AFTER COIN-THROWING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO GROUND BAN AFTER COIN-THROWING.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna were banned by Spanish soccer authorities on Tuesday from playing one match at their Riazor ground after a coin-throwing incident.
A referee was hit in the face by a coin thrown from the stands at the end of last week's home league game with Rayo Vallecano.
Club president Augusto Lendoiro said he would appeal against the decision, which he called "disproportionate". The team must play one game at another ground.
A 16-year-old boy arrested at the Rayo match has been banned from Deportivo fixtures for six months.
Sevilla were ordered to close their Sanchez Pizjuan stadium after a similar incident earlier this season, but have won a temporary reprieve pending an appeal hearing.
Both clubs have based their arguments against closure on the impossibility of stopping fans bringing coins to matches.
